subject: Phased region anchoring & dataflow clarifications — Acme Health
messages:
From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acmehealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 08:32:00 -0500
Subject: Residency anchoring + failover windows — follow up

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Before procurement moves this to legal we need a clear, scannable statement on two items so our security and privacy teams can sign off: 1) an EU-residency anchoring commitment for customer data at rest and processing (we'd like to see exact language you can put into the DPA addendum); and 2) operational behavior if a regional outage forces temporary cross-region processing — what are the triggers, maximum duration, and notification commitments?

We also need a current subprocessor roster (even if a snapshot) and to confirm whether any analytics telemetry ever leaves the EU for indexing. We attached a short questionnaire and the procurement contact for follow-up.

Can you confirm timelines? We need a procurement-ready answer by EOD Monday (16 Nov) to keep our target cutover.

Best,
Alice Wong
Head of Cloud Privacy — Acme Health

Attachment: acme-questionnaire.pdf (survey form)

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Residency anchoring + failover windows — follow up

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front, then a proposed next-step plan: 

1) EU anchoring language: we can provide an addendum paragraph for the DPA: "Redwood Inference will process and store Customer Data within the European Economic Area (EEA) for the duration of the agreement, except as expressly permitted in this Addendum or as required by law. Temporary cross‑region processing for the purposes of failover or disaster recovery will not exceed 72 hours without prior notice and Customer consent, except where emergency measures are required to preserve availability." (see caveat below).

2) Failover behavior: triggers include loss of region capacity (SRE-declared outage) or catastrophic hardware/network failures. We will: (a) attempt intra-region fallback to warm standby; (b) if forced cross-region, limit to anonymized telemetry where possible and restrict runtime data egress to the minimal tokens needed to complete in-flight requests; (c) notify your security contact within 2 hours and update hourly until cutover reversal. Max automatic transient window proposed: 72 hours; after that we require documented consent to continue.

3) Subprocessors & telemetry: attaching current roster snapshot (redacted for internal-only vendor IDs) — telemetry for service analytics is processed within the EEA for anchored customers. Non-PII logging used for capacity planning may be routed to our global analytics pipeline but can be suppressed per customer addendum.

Proposed next step: Marissa (legal) and Karthik (ops) — can you confirm acceptability of the DPA paragraph and the 72h transient window? If yes, I'll push a DPA addendum draft and link a DocuSign with trackable acceptance so procurement can proceed.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: subprocessor_roster_snapshot.csv (see attachments list)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Residency anchoring + failover windows — follow up

Jasmine — the proposed DPA language is a good starting point but Legal asks for two small edits to reduce ambiguity: 

- Replace "except as expressly permitted" with "except as expressly permitted in writing and in accordance with applicable law" to prevent broad interpretations.
- Clarify the scope of "Temporary cross-region processing" to explicitly exclude customer-requested disaster recovery testing (we'll document a separate test schedule).

On the 72h window: Legal is comfortable including that as a default operational limit for automated failover, provided we add a sentence requiring Redwood to provide a detailed incident report within 5 business days when a cross-region failover occurs. That incident report will include a timeline and what data paths were traversed.

I've attached a redline (Acme_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf) with exact wording. Also adding Jordan (platform PM) to confirm the telemetry suppression and ops notifications are implementable as described.

- Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Acme_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Residency anchoring + failover windows — follow up

Confirming operational feasibility. A few implementation notes for the customer: 

- EU anchoring: we can pin ingestion, primary KV cache and long-term object storage to EU-only nodes for the customer account. That covers data-at-rest and standard inference processing.
- Failover: our warm-standby model means most recoveries stay inside-region; true cross-region will require routing changes and KMS key access from the target region. We can enable a transient KMS wrap option for up to 72h but we need the customer to acknowledge the key-handling steps in the addendum (we'll provide a short key flow diagram).
- Telemetry suppression: ops can gate the analytics pipeline for the account to ensure no indexed traces leave the EU; this is a config flag on onboarding but requires a 48-hour ops lead time to fully validate.

I'll attach the short runbook excerpt (internal) that outlines the switches and the notification hook for customers. If Acme wants the 72h to be shorter (48h) we can talk SLA tradeoffs and pricing.

-Karthik
Director, Regional Ops

Attachment: runbook-excerpt.txt (internal ops steps)

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Residency anchoring + failover windows — follow up

Hi Alice — following up with a consolidated, procurement-ready package per your EOD Monday request. Items enclosed and next steps: 

1) Draft DPA addendum language (incorporates Marissa's legal edits) — link: https://app.redwood.ai/contracts/ACME-2026-88
2) Snapshot of current subprocessor roster (CSV attached) — we will provide a monthly roster cadence if that helps.
3) Ops commitments: 72-hour transient window with hourly notifications and a 5 business day incident report for any cross-region event. Ops will suppress analytics traces leaving the EEA; Karthik notes there is a 48-hour validation lead time for that config.

Action requested from Acme: please review the linked addendum and redlines and indicate whether you accept the 72-hour default or prefer a 48-hour cap (the latter may have pricing implications). If language is acceptable, Marissa will token the addendum for signature via DocuSign and procurement can execute.

I'll keep the loop open for any final questions — happy to hop on a 30-minute call with your security and procurement teams tomorrow morning if you'd like.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Acme_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf, subprocessor_roster_snapshot.csv
DocuSign draft queued: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/ACME-2026-88-draft
